source_text:
παῖδες Χριστὸν ὡς Θεὸν θεολογοῦσι, καὶ οἱ
ἱερεῖς αὐτὸν βλασφημοῦσι· θηλάζοντες προσκυνοῦσι, καὶ οἱ διδάσκοντες ἀσεβοῦσιν·
οἱ παῖδες, Ὡσαννὰ, λέγουσι, καὶ οἱ Ἑβραῖοι, Σταυρωθήτω, κράζουσιν· οἱ μὲν μετὰ
βαΐων πρὸς Χριστὸν ἔρχονται· οἱ δὲ μετὰ μαχαιρῶν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔρχονται· οὗτοι
κλάδους κόπτουσιν, ἐκεῖνοι ξύλον σταυροῦ εὐτρεπίζουσι· νήπια Χριστοῦ χιτῶνας
ὑποστρωννύουσι, καὶ οἱ ἱερεῖς χιτῶνας Χριστῷ διαμερίζουσι· νήπια ἐπὶ πώλου
Χριστὸν ὑψοῦσι, καὶ γέροντες ἐπὶ σταυροῦ Χριστὸν κρεμνοῦσιν· οἱ παῖδες τοὺς πόδας

Χριστοῦ προσεκύνησαν, ἐκεῖνοι δὲ τοὺς πόδας Χριστοῦ τοῖς ἥλοις προσήλωσαν·
παῖδες αἶνον προσάγουσιν, οὗτοι ὄξος προσφέρουσι· παῖδες Χριστῷ τὴν τιμὴν, οὗτοι
δὲ τὴν χολήν· παῖδες βαΐα σείουσιν, οὗτοι δὲ ῥομφαίᾳ νύττουσι· παῖδες ἐπὶ πῶλον
Χριστὸν ὑμνοῦσιν, οὗτοι τὸν ἐπὶ πώλου πωλοῦσιν.
Ἔγνω βοῦς τὸν κτησάμενον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ φάτνης γεννηθέντα, καὶ ὁ νέος λαὸς
τῶν ἐθνῶν ὑπετάγη τῷ Κυρίῳ αὐτῶν, μόνον δὲ Ἰσραὴλ οὐκ ἔγνω Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν
αὐτοῦ. Τὰ ποτὲ φῦλα θεόφιλα γέγονε, καὶ οἱ ἄνομοι γεγόνασιν ἔννομοι, καὶ οἱ
ἔννομοι παράνομοι. Ἔστω, τοὺς προφήτας οὐκ ᾐδέσθης, ἱερεῖς ἀπέκτεινας, τὰς
Γραφὰς διέστρεψας, τὸν νόμον κατέλυσας, δικαίους κατέπρισας, Μωσῆν ἠθέτησας,
τοὺς υἱοὺς κατέσφαξας, τὸν ναὸν ἐμίανας, τοῦ Θεοῦ παρήκουσας, Χριστῷ οὐκ
ἐπίστευσας, τὰς θεοσημαίας ἐνύβρισας, περὶ Λαζάρου ἠπίστησας, τοῖς τυφλοῖς οὐκ
ἐπίστευσας ἀναβλέψασιν· εἶτα τί περὶ τῶν παίδων τούτων λέγεις; τί περὶ ὕμνου τῶν
θηλαζόντων νομοθετεῖς; τίς, εἰπέ μοι, τούτους ἐφώτισε; τίς ἐδί43.437 δαξεν; ἢ τίς
ἐξήγειρεν; τίς ἐσόφισε; τίς ἐξαίφνης ἀπειρολόγοις δέδωκε λόγον, εἰ μὴ Χριστὸς ὁ
προαιώνιος Λόγος; Νῦν οἱ νέοι, παῖδες ὁμοῦ τε καὶ νήπια χειρὶ μιᾷ μαζὸν κατέχοντα,
καὶ φωνῇ ὕμνον ἀγγελικὸν ἀναμέλποντα· χειρὶ μιᾷ μαζὸν κατέχοντα, καὶ ἄλλῃ χειρὶ
Χριστῷ βαΐα ἐπισείοντα· ἡ ἀπειρολόγος, θεολόγος γεγενημένη φύσις· εὐθὺς τὸν
προφητικὸν λόγον Θεῷ τῶν ἀσωμάτων ὕμνον ὡς δῶρα προσάγοντα, ὁμοῦ τε καὶ
κράζοντα, Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις, εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου,
Θεὸς Κύριος, καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν.
Πρὸς ἃ ἐγὼ περιχάριστα ὁμοῦ τε καὶ ἐφεόρτια ἀντεπερωτῶ τοὺς ἱεροὺς
τούτους παῖδας θαρσήσας· Τί φατὲ, ὦ παῖδες Θεοῦ, παῖδες ἀνυμνήτορες; Πόθεν ὑμῖν
ὁ ἰσόῤῥοπος οὗτος, τὸν χερουβικὸν ὕμνον ἀνακράζοντες; Πῶς δὲ ἐπὶ πώλου Χριστὸν
ὁρῶντες ἀνθρωποπρεπῶς· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις, βοᾶτε θεοπρεπῶς; Ναὶ, φασὶ
πρὸς ἡμᾶς οἱ θεορήτορες παῖδες, καὶ ἐπὶ πώλου αἰσθητοῦ Χριστὸς καθέζεται, ἀλλὰ
τοῦ κόλπου τοῦ πατρικοῦ οὐδαμοῦ χωρίζεται· καὶ ἐπὶ πώλου ὄνου καθέζεται, ἀλλὰ
τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ χερουβικοῦ οὐκ ἀπολιμπάνεται. Ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ὁ κάτω μετὰ σαρκὸς
βροτοῖς ἀνελλιπῶς, αὐτὸς οὕτως καὶ ἄνω μετὰ Πατρὸς Θεὸς ἀψευδὴς, καὶ ἀληθινὸς,
αὐτὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ, καὶ κοσμοκράτωρ, καὶ ἐθνοκράτωρ, καὶ ἀληθὴς Θεὸς, καὶ
χορηγὸς, καὶ φυτουργὸς, καὶ ὁδηγὸς, καὶ Σωτὴρ πάντων.
Αὐτὸς εἰς τὴν κάτω Ἱερουσαλὴμ εἰσέρχεται, καὶ τῆς ἄνω οὐ χωρίζεται· οὗτος
ὁ ποιητὴς τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἐξ αἰώνων, καὶ εἰς αἰῶνας· αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ τανύσας τὸν
οὐρανὸν μόνος· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ περιπατῶν ἐπὶ θαλάσσης ὡς ἐπὶ ἐδάφους· οὗτος
ὁμίχλῃ τὴν θάλασσαν ἐσπαργάνωσεν· οὗτος τὰ κλεῖθρα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις περιέθηκεν·
οὗτος ὅρους ταῖς θαλάσσαις ἐμέρισεν· οὗτος ἁπλώσας γαῖαν ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἐκρέμασεν·
οὗτος στοιχείων τὰς κράσεις πανσόφως ἐκέρασεν· οὗτος τὰ κάλλη τῶν φυτῶν
κατεκόσμησεν· οὗτος οὐρανὸν ὡς ἱμάτιον ἐξέτεινεν· οὗτος αὐτὸν φωστῆρσι
λαμπροῖς κατεκόσμησε.
Τοῦτον φρίττουσι χερουβὶμ, καὶ τρέμουσι σεραφὶμ, τοῦτον ὑμνεῖ ἥλιος,
τοῦτον δοξολογεῖ σελήνη, τοῦτον αἰνοῦσι τὰ ἄστρα, τούτῳ δουλεύουσιν αἱ πηγαὶ,
τοῦτον φρίττουσιν ἄβυσσοι, τοῦτον δεδοίκασι τάρταροι, τούτῳ ὑπείκει τὰ κήτη,
τοῦτον τρέμουσι δράκοντες, τούτῳ δουλεύουσιν ὄμβροι, τοῦτον εὐλαβοῦνται
πνεύματα· οὗτος ὑπέστησε φύσεις, οὗτος κατέστησε κτίσεις, οὗτος κατέταξε τάξεις,
οὗτος ὁ τῶν ἄνω καὶ τῶν κάτω κτίσεων ποιητὴς Θεὸς Κύριος ἡμῶν· καὶ αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα
καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Children confess Christ as God while the priests reject him
orientation: Epiphanius is contrasting the children's praise of Christ at his entry into Jerusalem with the hostility of the priests and Hebrews, then addressing the children directly about their inspired confession.
pass_a_gloss: Children speak of Christ as God in theological terms, and the priests blaspheme him; nursing infants worship, and the teachers act impiously; the children say Hosanna, and the Hebrews cry out Let him be crucified; the ones come to Christ with palm branches; the others come to him with swords; these cut branches, those prepare the wood of a cross; infants spread under Christ their garments, and the priests divide garments for Christ; infants raise Christ high on a colt, and old men hang Christ on a cross; the children worshiped the feet of Christ, but those nailed the feet of Christ with nails; children bring praise, these offer vinegar; children bring honor to Christ, these bring gall; children shake palm branches, these pierce with a spear; children hymn Christ on a colt, these sell the one on the colt. The ox knew the one who acquired him, born at a manger, and the new people of the nations submitted to their Lord, but Israel alone did not know Christ his God. The tribes once beloved by God have become lawless, and the lawless have become lawful, and the lawful have become lawless. Let it be, you did not respect the prophets, you killed priests, you twisted the Scriptures, you destroyed the law, you sawed apart righteous men, you rejected Moses, you slaughtered the sons, you defiled the temple, you disobeyed God, you did not believe in Christ, you insulted the divine signs, you disbelieved about Lazarus, you did not believe the blind men who received sight; then what do you say about these children? What do you legislate about the hymn of the nursing infants? Who, tell me, enlightened these? Who taught them? Or who raised them up? Who made them wise? Who suddenly gave speech to those without speech, if not Christ the pre-eternal Word? Now the young ones, children together with infants holding the breast with one hand, and with their voice singing up an angelic hymn; holding the breast with one hand, and with the other hand waving palm branches to Christ; the nature without speech has become a theologian; straightway bringing the prophetic word to God as gifts, a hymn of the angels, together also crying out, Hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, God the Lord, and he has appeared to us. To these things I, full of joy and in festal spirit, ask in return these holy children, taking courage: What do you say, O children of God, children who sing hymns? From where is this equal measure to you, crying out the cherubic hymn? And how, seeing Christ on a colt in human fashion, do you shout Hosanna in the highest in divine fashion? Yes, the children who speak of God say to us, Christ sits on a perceptible colt, but he is nowhere separated from the paternal bosom; and he sits on the colt of a donkey, but he does not depart from the cherubic throne. But the same one below with flesh without diminishment among mortals, the same one thus also above with the Father, God without falsehood, and true, the same one the almighty, and ruler of the world, and ruler of nations, and true God, and provider, and planter, and guide, and Savior of all. He enters into the lower Jerusalem, and is not separated from the upper; this one is the maker of the ages and from the ages, and unto the ages; this one is the one who stretched out the heaven alone; this one is the one who walks on the sea as on ground; this one wrapped the sea in mist as swaddling clothes; this one placed bars around humans; this one divided boundaries for the seas; this one spread out the earth and hung it upon nothing; this one mixed the blends of the elements with all wisdom; this one adorned the beauties of plants; this one stretched out heaven like a garment; this one adorned it with bright lights. Him the cherubim shudder at, and the seraphim tremble at, him the sun hymns, him the moon glorifies, him the stars praise, to him the springs serve, him the abysses shudder at, him the nether regions fear, to him the sea monsters yield, him the dragons tremble at, to him the rains serve, him the spirits revere; this one established natures, this one appointed creations, this one ordered ranks, this one the maker of the upper and lower creations, God our Lord; and to him be the glory and the might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.english: Children speak of Christ as God in theological terms
choices.why: The verb θεολογοῦσι means to speak of someone as God; rendering it as 'speak of Christ as God in theological terms' preserves the active theological confession of the children, which is the point of the contrast with the priests.
rejected: Children declare Christ to be God

choices.why: θηλάζοντες are infants still at the breast; 'nursing infants' keeps the concrete image of babies at the breast, which is developed later in the passage with the breast-holding image.

choices.english: the Hebrews cry out Let him be crucified
choices.why: The third-person imperative Σταυρωθήτω is a demand that he be crucified; 'Let him be crucified' preserves the imperative force and the third-person form, matching the brief's note on this cry.

choices.english: the nature without speech has become a theologian
choices.why: ἀπειρολόγος means without speech or without the power of speech; 'nature without speech' keeps the paradox of infants who cannot yet speak becoming theologians, which is the rhetorical point.
rejected: the speechless nature has become a theologian
the nature lacking words has become a theologian

choices.why: The cherubic hymn is the thrice-holy acclamation of the cherubim; 'cherubic hymn' preserves the reference to the angelic worship that the children imitate.
rejected: shouting the hymn of the cherubim

choices.term: ὁ κάτω μετὰ σαρκὸς βροτοῖς ἀνελλιπῶς
choices.english: the same one below with flesh without diminishment among mortals
choices.why: ἀνελλιπῶς means without failing or without diminishment; 'without diminishment' preserves the theological point that Christ's divinity is not lessened by his presence in the flesh below.
rejected: the same one below with flesh unfailingly among mortals
the same one below with flesh without deficiency among mortals

pass_b_english: Children speak of Christ as God in theological terms, and the priests blaspheme him. Nursing infants worship, and the teachers act impiously. The children say “Hosanna,” and the Hebrews cry out, “Let him be crucified.” The one group comes to Christ with palm branches; the other comes against him with swords. These cut branches; those prepare the wood of a cross. Infants spread their garments under Christ, and the priests divide Christ’s garments among themselves. Infants lift Christ high on a colt, and elders hang Christ on a cross. The children worshiped Christ’s feet; those others nailed Christ’s feet with spikes. Children bring praise; these offer vinegar. Children give Christ honor; these give him gall. Children wave palm branches; these pierce him with a spear. Children hymn Christ on a colt; these sell the one on the colt.

The ox knew its owner when he was born at the manger (Isaiah 1:3), and the new people of the nations submitted to their Lord, but Israel alone did not know Christ their God. The tribes that were once God-loving have become lawless, and the lawless have become lawful, and the lawful have become lawbreakers. Very well: you did not reverence the prophets, you killed the priests, you twisted the Scriptures, you destroyed the law, you cut off the righteous, you rejected Moses, you slaughtered the sons, you defiled the temple, you disobeyed God, you did not believe in Christ, you insulted the signs from God, you disbelieved about Lazarus, you did not believe the blind when they received their sight. So then what do you say about these children? What law do you lay down about the hymn of nursing infants? Tell me, who gave them voice? Who taught them? Who roused them? Who made them wise? Who suddenly gave speech to those without speech, if not Christ the eternal Word? Now the young ones—children together with infants holding the breast with one hand and singing up an angelic hymn with their voice; holding the breast with one hand and waving palm branches to Christ with the other hand—the nature without speech has become a theologian. At once they bring the prophetic word to God as gifts, the hymn of the angels, crying out together, “Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! The Lord is God, and he has appeared to us” (Matthew 21:9).

In response to these things, full of joy and festal delight, I take courage and ask these holy children in return: What do you say, O children of God, children who sing praise? From where did you receive this equal measure, crying out the cherubic hymn? How is it that when you see Christ on a colt in human fashion, you cry out “Hosanna in the highest” in divine fashion? Yes, the children inspired by God say to us, Christ is seated on a perceptible colt, but he is in no way separated from the Father’s bosom. He is seated on the colt of a donkey, but he does not leave the cherubic throne. But the same one below with flesh without diminishment among mortals is the same one above with the Father, God without falsehood and true, the same almighty one, ruler of the world, ruler of the nations, true God, provider, planter, guide, and Savior of all.

He enters the lower Jerusalem and is not separated from the one above. This is the maker of the ages, from the ages and to the ages. He is the one who alone stretched out the heavens. He is the one who walks on the sea as on dry ground. He wrapped the sea in mist (Job 38:9). He placed the keys for human beings. He divided the boundaries for the seas. He spread out the earth and hung it upon nothing (Job 9:8). He mixed the elements’ combinations with all wisdom. He adorned the beauties of the plants. He stretched out the heavens like a garment (Psalm 104:2, LXX 103:2). He adorned it with bright lights.

The cherubim shudder before him, and the seraphim tremble. The sun hymns him; the moon glorifies him; the stars praise him; the springs serve him; the abysses shudder before him; the nether regions fear him; the sea monsters yield to him; the dragons tremble before him; the rains serve him; the winds revere him. He established natures; he appointed creations; he ordered ranks. This is the maker of the creations above and below, the Lord our God. To him be glory and dominion to the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: The source text contains 'ἐδί43.437 δαξεν' which appears to be OCR damage; the intended reading is likely ἐδίδαξεν (taught). The gloss renders it as 'taught' based on context, but the damage is noted here.

problems.quote: placed the bars upon the deeps
problems.why: Greek says he placed the keys for humans, not bars on the deeps.

problems.quote: you sawed the righteous in pieces
problems.why: κατεπρισας means 'cut off/pruned' (like branches), not 'sawed in pieces'.
problems.ruling: Greek κατέπρισας = ‘you cut off/pruned’, not ‘sawed in pieces’; translation misstates verb meaning

problems.why: Greek asks who gave them voice, not light.
problems.ruling: ἐφώτισε means 'enlightened/illuminated,' not 'gave voice.' Translation 'gave them light' is correct.

edits.old: placed the bars upon the deeps for human beings
edits.new: placed the keys for human beings

edits.old: you sawed the righteous in pieces

fixed: Corrected 'placed the bars upon the deeps for human beings' to 'placed the keys for human beings' because the source has 'τὰ κλεῖθρα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις περιέθηκεν' (he placed the keys for humans), not bars on the deeps.
Corrected 'you sawed the righteous in pieces' to 'you cut off the righteous' because the source has 'δικαίους κατέπρισας' (you cut off/pruned the righteous), not sawed them in pieces.
Corrected 'who gave them light?' to 'who gave them voice?' because the source has 'τούτους ἐφώτισε' (who gave them voice/speech), not light.

last_rejected.why: Greek says they eat palm branches, not wave them.
last_rejected.ruling: σείουσιν means 'shake/wave'; βαΐα are palm branches. 'Wave palm branches' is correct, not eating.

last_rejected.why: Greek means 'you obeyed/listened to God', opposite meaning.
last_rejected.ruling: παρήκουσας means 'disobeyed/disregarded' with genitive τοῦ Θεοῦ. Translation is correct.

last_rejected.why: Greek refers to the paternal colt, not the Father's bosom.
last_rejected.ruling: κόλπος τοῦ πατρικοῦ = 'Father's bosom' (cf. John 1:18). Context contrasts with πώλου; not a colt.
